name: Museu de Belles Arts de Castelló
key_features: Metal-clad gallery block whose stepped rooftop lanterns light the rooms, joined to an older building around a patio.

name: Seville–Santa Justa Station
key_features: Brick station under a long curved concrete canopy, opening onto a high vaulted platform hall.

name: La Ricarda (Casa Gomis)
key_features: Pavilion house of thin concrete vaults on a modular grid, spread among pine trees near the sea.

name: Pavilion of Knowledge (Pavilhão do Conhecimento)
key_features: White science museum around an open patio, its long upper block cantilevered over the court.

name: Nadir Afonso Contemporary Art Museum
key_features: Long white concrete museum lifted on piers above the riverside meadow.

name: Setúbal School of Education
key_features: Low white school around a U-shaped lawn, lined by a deep colonnade.

name: Matosinhos Town Hall
key_features: Stone-clad town hall with long colonnades, set back behind a row of poplars on a civic square.

name: Riverside Centre
key_features: 40-storey office tower above an open riverfront plaza with steps, cafés and a ferry wharf.

name: Melbourne School of Design (Glyn Davis Building)
key_features: Architecture school built as a teaching tool: exposed structure and a studio hall under a coffered timber roof.

name: Ian Potter Museum of Art
key_features: University art museum whose grey street wall carries a frieze of broken classical fragments.

name: Institute for Marine and Antarctic Studies
key_features: Waterfront research 'shed' on Princes Wharf, its long folded roof lifting into a glazed end towards the harbour.

name: Art Gallery of New South Wales, North Building (Sydney Modern, Naala Nura)
key_features: Glass pavilions under thin roofs step down to Woolloomooloo Bay; a disused oil tank below became 'The Tank' gallery.

name: Green Square Library and Plaza
key_features: Library sunk below a public plaza; only a glass tower, a triangular skylight and sunken garden rise above ground.

name: National Library of Australia
key_features: Stripped Classical library on Lake Burley Griffin: a colonnade of slim columns under a flat roof, marble foyer inside.

name: Mobilier National
key_features: Perret's 1937 home of the state furniture workshops: concrete used with classical symmetry and proportion.

name: Halle Tony Garnier
key_features: Steel roof truss on ball-and-socket joints leaves the 80 x 210 m former cattle hall free of columns.

name: Santa Maria Consolatrice al Tiburtino
key_features: Minimalist parish church begun in 1942 and consecrated in 1945, on Piazza Santa Maria Consolatrice.

name: Embassy of Denmark, London
key_features: Called a stark architectural grid of grey modernism, with a geometric concrete mural by Ole Schwalbe.

name: Southwark tube station
key_features: Jubilee line station whose upper concourse is the centrepiece, with a 40 m glass wall of 660 blue glass pieces.

name: Gorilla House, London Zoo
key_features: White cylindrical drum in 10 cm reinforced concrete, with a rotating semi-circular top-hung screen.

name: Sun House
key_features: Modernist house on Frognal Way, Hampstead; Grade II* listed.

name: Kleinhans Music Hall
key_features: Concert hall by father and son with two performance spaces; a National Historic Landmark for its architecture.

name: Power Center for the Performing Arts
by: Kevin Roche John Dinkeloo and Associates
key_features: Proscenium-stage theatre on the University of Michigan's central campus, opened 1971.

name: Evans Hall
key_features: Statistics, economics and maths building known for many windowless classrooms.

name: Freeway Park
key_features: Built over Interstate 5 and a parking lot; blends brutalist architecture with greenery.

name: Théâtre Maisonneuve
key_features: 1,453-seat theatre in the Place des Arts complex, inaugurated 1967.

name: Erasmus Bridge
key_features: 802 m cable-stayed and bascule bridge; Ben van Berkel's design has one backward-leaning pylon.

name: Silodam
key_features: Housing and mixed-use complex on a former breakwater beside the 1890s Stone Silo; 95 homes in a container-like stack.

name: Supreme Court of Singapore
key_features: Disc-shaped Court of Appeal on the ninth storey, and extensive glass atria and skylights meant to signify transparency.

name: Sultan Mosque
key_features: Two gold onion domes decorated with glass bottle ends, and two eight-storey minarets on the east facade.

name: North Christian Church
key_features: 192-foot-tall church with interiors by Alexander Girard and landscape by Dan Kiley.

name: Riyadh TV Tower
key_features: 170 m television tower, Saudi Arabia's tallest structure until 2000.

name: National Library of Armenia
key_features: Main building follows Tamanian's project; the 'Tamanyan style' reinterprets medieval Armenian architecture.

name: Matarazzo Building (São Paulo City Hall)
key_features: Italian rationalist design resembling Art Deco; now São Paulo's city hall.

name: Palace of Justice of São Paulo
by: Francisco Ramos de Azevedo, Ricardo Severo, Arnaldo Villares
key_features: One of Brazil's first buildings with a metal structure, mixing baroque and neoclassical elements.

name: San Javier Library Park
key_features: One of Medellín's ten library parks, in the San Javier area; opened December 2006.

name: León de Greiff Library Park
key_features: Library park by Giancarlo Mazzanti in Medellín, opened February 2007.

name: National Library of Venezuela
key_features: Brutalist national library in Caracas, designed 1981-1989.

name: Islamic Summit Minar
key_features: 47 m marble and stone obelisk beside a reflecting pool, with an underground museum, for the 1974 Islamic Summit.

name: Lahore Museum
by: Bhai Ram Singh and John Lockwood Kipling
key_features: Indo-Saracenic red-brick museum housing Gandharan and Indus Valley collections, plus Sadequain's ceiling mural.

name: Japan Ukiyo-e Museum
key_features: Private museum holding over 100,000 woodblock prints, the largest collection of its kind.

name: Miyagi Museum of Art
key_features: Collection centres on Miyagi and Tohoku artists, with works by Kandinsky and Klee.

name: Hashima City Hall (1959)
key_features: Town hall of 1959 by Junzo Sakakura; the building was demolished in 2022.

name: Okayama Prefectural Government Office Main Building
key_features: Prefectural government office beside Okayama Castle, listed among Kunio Maekawa's works of 1955.

name: Nima Sand Museum
key_features: Sand museum in Nima, Oda, listed among Shin Takamatsu's works of 1990.

name: Iida City Museum
key_features: Museum of the area's natural history, history and art, opened in 1989.

name: Miyagi Prefectural Library
key_features: Prefectural library in Sendai, listed among Hiroshi Hara's works of 1998.

name: Okayama Symphony Hall
key_features: Concert hall of 2,001 seats, with acoustic design by Nagata Acoustics.

name: Mercedes-Benz Arena (Expo Culture Center)
key_features: Nicknamed 'the Clam Shell' and 'the Hamburger'; the arena seats 18,000.

name: Peter B. Lewis Building (Weatherhead School of Management)
key_features: Gehry's 2002 business school: about 150,000 sq ft over five stories, offices and classrooms mixed on every floor.

name: Fire Station No. 4, Columbus
by: Robert Venturi and Denise Scott Brown (Venturi and Rauch)
key_features: Trapezoid plan; a semicircular entrance tower topped with a large yellow number 4.

name: Vitra Conference Pavilion
key_features: Tadao Ando's first building outside Japan; gridded concrete and holes for light define its style.

name: Esbjerg Performing Arts Centre
key_features: Concert hall designed by Jan Utzon with his father Jørn Utzon, beside the Art Museum in the City Park.

name: Landskrona City Hall
key_features: Modernist city hall by the new harbour, inaugurated in September 1976.

name: Lillehammer Art Museum
key_features: Snøhetta's wing, opened 1992, joins an older building by Erling Viksjø.

name: Kunstnernes Hus
key_features: Artists' House, a prominent Functionalist building, opened on 1 October 1930.

name: Museum of Central Finland
key_features: Cultural history museum in a building designed by Alvar Aalto, completed in 1960.

name: Ympyrätalo
key_features: Circle-shaped building in Hakaniemi, opened 1968 and renovated 2002–2004.

name: Uspenski Cathedral
key_features: Orthodox cathedral in Russian Revival style, built 1862–1868 under Ivan Varnek.

name: National Theatre of Iceland
key_features: National theatre, formally opened on 20 April 1950.

name: Itatiaia Building
key_features: Campinas's first Modernist building, by Oscar Niemeyer, often compared with Copan in São Paulo.

name: Torre Realia BCN
key_features: Toyo Ito's 24-floor, 112-metre tower on Plaça d'Europa, L'Hospitalet, completed in 2009.

name: Onomichi City Museum of Art
key_features: Tadao Ando's 2003 redesign of Onomichi's art museum in Senkō-ji Park, first opened in 1980.

name: Hochhaus Neue Donau
key_features: Harry Seidler's 34-storey residential tower in Vienna's Donau City, 150 metres tall and currently Austria's third tallest building.

name: Mode Gakuen Spiral Towers
key_features: Nagoya's 170-metre, 36-storey school tower, home to three vocational schools and one of the city's tallest buildings.

name: Sinan Pasha Mosque (Istanbul)
key_features: Sinan's mosque in Beşiktaş, built for Admiral Sinan Pasha, with Barbaros Hayrettin Pasha's tomb across the street.

name: Frank Lloyd Wright Home and Studio
key_features: Wright's home and studio in Oak Park, built in 1889 and expanded with a Prairie-style studio.

name: Otaniemi water tower
key_features: Aalto's 1971 water tower in Otaniemi, a 45-metre landmark stacking a water tank on a free-form building.

name: Waldspirale
key_features: Hundertwasser's 2000 Darmstadt housing complex, with a spiral plan and a green roof.

name: Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology
key_features: Lisbon's museum of art, architecture and technology, a 2016 work by Amanda Levete (AL_A).

name: Hansahochhaus
key_features: Cologne's first skyscraper and one of Germany's first, an Expressionist office building built 1924–25.

name: Perelman Performing Arts Center
key_features: Joshua Ramus's performing arts center on the World Trade Center site, chosen in 2015 after earlier plans were scrapped.

name: Tournay Abbey
key_features: An active Benedictine monastery of about 20 monks; the new building was completed in 1958.

name: Museum Yamato Bunkakan
key_features: Museum of Asian art in Nara, established in 1960 for the private collection of the Kintetsu railway company.

name: Minnaert building
by: Neutelings Riedijk Architects, Willem Jan Neutelings, Michiel Riedijk
key_features: Campus building named after astronomer Marcel Minnaert, opened in 1997 for Utrecht University's science faculties.

name: Paraninfo de la Universidad del País Vasco
key_features: Álvaro Siza's 2010 hall for the Basque Country university, faced in grey handmade tiles and white marble.

name: Kita des Deutschen Bundestages
key_features: Peichl's Berlin nursery for Bundestag families, shaped like a ship moored on the Spree, with lively colour.

name: Fukuoka Camera Museum
key_features: Tadao Ando's camera and photography museum in Takaoka, Toyama.

name: Hagi Uragami Museum
key_features: A prefectural art museum in Hagi, one of several cultural facilities planned to be spread evenly across Yamaguchi Prefecture.

name: ONIKURU
key_features: A civic complex in Ibaraki with a hall, library, children's centre, indoor playground and planetarium.

name: Skylight
key_features: A 'city within a city' in Frankfurt: offices, shops and flats around a 66-metre residential tower.

name: Konzerthaus Blaibach
key_features: Concert house in the village of Blaibach in the Upper Palatinate, for concerts, cultural events and exhibitions.

name: Villa of Viktor Bauer
key_features: Loos's puristic villa for a sugar-refinery director in Hrušovany, the only large Loos work in Moravia.

name: Haus Scheu
key_features: Loos's Vienna house, one of the first modern buildings to use a flat roof.

name: Vakantiehuisjes (Rietveld)
key_features: One of six Rietveld cottages of 1951 for factory staff; one was moved to the Arnhem open-air museum.

name: Palazzo degli Affari
key_features: Carlo Mollino's Turin chamber of commerce offices, a bold structural solution set against its surroundings.

name: Offenbarungskirche
key_features: One of the postwar emergency churches (Notkirchen) by Bauhaus-trained Otto Bartning, part of a community centre.

name: Ruderzentrum Blasewitz
key_features: A rowing centre roofed by four hyperbolic paraboloid shells, tilted inwards to let in more daylight.

name: Villa Haas
key_features: A functionalist villa in Brno's Pisárky district, built 1928–1930 for the head of a bank branch.

name: Église Sainte-Thérèse-de-l'Enfant-Jésus de Metz
key_features: Roger-Henri Expert's church in Metz, with stained glass by Nicolas Untersteller in a personal, new technique.

name: Naturtheater Grötzingen
key_features: A 1954 thin concrete shell over an open-air sylvan theatre that seats 850.

name: Vila Franze Strosse
key_features: A 1923–25 villa in Liberec by Thilo Schoder, its rounded forms evoking a ship.

name: International Conference Center Hiroshima
key_features: A convention centre with a multipurpose hall in central Hiroshima, designed by Kenzō Tange.

name: ONYX theater
key_features: A performance venue in Saint-Herblain, created in 1988 and now run by the city.

name: Vila Tychonova 4
key_features: The southern half of a double villa in Prague's Hradčany by Josef Gočár, protected since 1958.

name: Hochhaus Württembergische Straße 6
key_features: West Berlin's first office high-rise, a pioneering example of postwar modernism with open, transparent architecture.

name: Schönberg Tower
key_features: A 26.4 m lookout tower from 1905 by the well-known architect Theodor Fischer, a landmark of Pfullingen.

name: Suchardova vila
key_features: Jan Kotěra's villa and studio for the sculptor Stanislav Sucharda and his family, built 1904–1907 in Prague.

name: St. Mauritius
key_features: A Brutalist church centre in Munich's Moosach district, completed in 1967.

name: Shikoku Mura Gallery
key_features: Ando's gallery on a hillside in Shikoku Mura, with a water garden and a view over Takamatsu.

name: Postgebouw van Oostende
key_features: Ostend's former post office, built 1947–1953 by Gaston Eysselinck and now a cultural centre.

name: Königliche Anatomie
key_features: Among the first large reinforced-concrete buildings in Germany, built 1905–1907 by Max Littmann.

name: Villa Carl (Feldafing)
key_features: Riemerschmid's 1910–12 Jugendstil villa in Feldafing, with its fully preserved original interior.

name: Villa Kroha
key_features: Architect Jiří Kroha's own functionalist family house in Brno, built 1928–1930.

name: Villa Patočka
key_features: Jiří Kroha's 1935–36 functionalist villa in Brno's Pod vodojemem colony.

name: Nymble
key_features: The KTH student union house in Stockholm, built 1928–1930 by Markelius and Åhrén and marked as culturally valuable in 2012.

name: Koumi-machi Kōgen Museum of Art
key_features: A town-run art museum in Koumi.
